subject: RE: Greenleaf Pharma - request: subprocessor inventory, dataflow & SIG evidence

Subject: Request: subprocessor inventory, dataflow diagram & SIG evidence

Hi Priyom / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Greenleaf is finalizing our vendor review for an upcoming procurement and we need the following to close the security review:

- Completed SIG questionnaire (we attached the template) with any open riser notes.
- A current subprocessor inventory (including region, type of service, and whether data is encrypted at rest).
- An annotated dataflow diagram showing where PHI/PII (sensitive customer data) may touch Redwood systems and which subprocessors see tokenized/pseudonymized data vs. raw data.
- Copy of your most recent SOC 2 report or SOC 2 letter and your SOC 2 auditor contact.

Our internal deadline is Wednesday, Aug 26 EOD PT. Can you confirm whether this timeline is feasible and whether you prefer we run the SIG in our portal or accept your native exports?

Thanks,

Sofia Ramos
Senior Information Security Manager
Greenleaf Pharma

1) I’ll attach our current subprocessor inventory (CSV) and a PDF annotation of the primary dataflow showing tokenization boundaries and where encryption is applied.
2) We’ll export our SIG answers and highlight any control gaps; if you prefer to import to your portal, we can provide both the native export and a completed XLSX.
3) SOC 2: I’ll share a read-only link to our SOC 2 report and the auditor contact. If you need an NDA or additional access guardrails, let me know.

Proposed next step: quick 20-min call Monday morning (Aug 24) to walk through the diagram and any tight questions. Is 10:00 AM PT OK?

Deliverables attached: redwood_subprocessors_aug2026.csv, dataflow_annotation_v1.pdf (interim). Final annotated diagram and completed SIG export to follow.

Best,

Priyom — quick clarifying note for the SIG answers and the dataflow:

- Token retention: Greenleaf is calling out retention of raw customer payloads. We should explicitly state our default retention period, the optional customer-configured retention, and which subprocessors (e.g., analytics, logging) get redacted vs. full content.
- KMS / key management: call out KMS provider and HSM usage for private deployments.
- Subprocessor status: mark whether subprocessors are covered under our master contract or require separate DPA addendums.

I can take ownership of the CAIQ/KMS sections and draft the SIG comments. Grace, can you confirm whether the audit logs (retention and access controls) section needs an updated retention policy excerpt?

—Karthik
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: subprocessor inventory, dataflow diagram & SIG evidence

Hi Sofia — attaching the final package per our plan. Summary of what’s included and where to find it: 

1) Subprocessor inventory (CSV) — redwood_subprocessors_aug2026.csv: lists vendor, service category, region(s), data access level, encryption at rest (yes/no), contractual coverage (master DPA or addendum).
2) Annotated dataflow — dataflow_annotated_v2.pdf: clearly labels where customer identifiers and sensitive content may be present, notes where tokenization/pseudonymization occurs, and flags subprocessors that receive derivatives (analytics/metrics) vs. raw content.
3) SOC 2 report (read-only link and PDF stub) — SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf + https://redwood.com/security/soc2/2025-report. Note: full report requires an NDA for download; let me know if you want the auditor contact.
4) SIG export — we included both the native JSON export in the Drive folder and a completed XLSX formatted to your template. Link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/Greenleaf_SIG_responses_v1

A few callouts for your review:
- Retention: default raw payload retention is 30 days unless a customer-configured retention is specified. We redact full content for analytics; logging retains metadata for 90 days.
- KMS: Hosted customers use AWS KMS with envelope encryption; Private customers can use customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations (we note the provider in the subprocessor row).
- Exceptions: A small set of legacy subprocessors are on addenda; we flagged those in the CSV.

If Greenleaf prefers we upload the completed SIG directly into your portal, we can do that once you confirm the import format. Otherwise the Drive folder contains everything for manual review. Happy to jump on the Monday 10:00 AM PT call to walk through any questions.

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

— Priyom Das
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
Attachments: dataflow_annotated_v2.pdf; SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf; redwood_subprocessors_aug2026.csv
